units: Mg C / ha (metric tonnes of carbon per hectare); NOT tonnes of biomass and NOT CO2e
definition: Carbon stored per hectare in each of four pools for a land-cover class: c_above = aboveground live biomass, c_below = belowground live biomass (roots), c_soil = soil organic carbon (to a stated depth, commonly 0-30 cm), c_dead = dead organic matter (litter + standing/downed deadwood). InVEST Carbon multiplies these by class area; sequestration is the difference between two LULC maps.

how_to_estimate.summary: Best: local forest-inventory / soil-survey data. Tier 1: IPCC default biomass by climate domain and forest type x 0.47 carbon fraction for c_above; a root-to-shoot ratio for c_below; an IPCC reference soil organic carbon stock modified by land-use / management / input factors for c_soil; an IPCC dead-organic-matter default for c_dead. Or use a ready spatial product (Ruesch & Gibbs 2008) for the biomass pools.
steps: c_above = (IPCC default aboveground biomass, t d.m./ha for your climate domain + forest type or non-forest class) x 0.47
c_below = c_above x (root-to-shoot ratio R for that vegetation type)  [grassland R can exceed 1]
c_soil = (IPCC reference SOC stock 0-30 cm for climate x soil type) x F_landuse x F_management x F_input   [F = 1 for native vegetation]
c_dead = IPCC Tier-1 dead-organic-matter default (litter + deadwood); often 0 for cropland/grassland, 2-8 for forest, higher in boreal

methods.name: IPCC 2006 Tier-1 defaults
methods.notes: Vol 4: Table 4.7 (AGB natural forest), 4.4 (R:S), 4.3 (carbon fraction 0.47), 2.3 (reference SOC), 5.5 & 6.2 (stock-change factors).

methods.name: IPCC 2019 refinement
methods.notes: Updated, more disaggregated biomass and SOC tables with uncertainty. Prefer where a matching row exists.

methods.name: spatial Tier-1 biomass map
methods.notes: Global c_above + c_below by land cover x ecofloristic zone x continent; lets carbon vary in space without a hand table.

how_to_choose: Fix the climate domain (tropical / subtropical / warm-temperate / cool-temperate / boreal) and moisture regime for your study area first - it drives every pool. Then match forest type (broadleaf/needleleaf, moist/dry, primary/secondary/plantation) and, for c_soil, the dominant soil type and land-use history. State the SOC depth you used (InVEST is indifferent but comparisons must match). All values below are Tier-1 order-of-magnitude with wide uncertainty (IPCC reports +/- 30-75%); treat as starting points, refine with any local inventory. Carbon fraction 0.47 unless a local value is known.

context.region: global Tier-1 (varies by continent - Africa highest AGB, America/Asia lower)
context.assumptions: AGB ~275 t d.m./ha x 0.47; R:S 0.24-0.37; SOC LAC/HAC tropical moist

records.caveats: Continental spread is large. Secondary / logged tropical forest c_above is 30-60% of this. Use the 2019 refinement or a regional biomass map if available.
records.provenance: standard reference (added; not in FS28 masterfile)

context.region: global Tier-1 (SE Australian temperate eucalypt forest fits here)
context.assumptions: AGB ~140 t d.m./ha x 0.47; R:S 0.24; SOC temperate moist HAC/LAC

records.caveats: Australian tall wet eucalypt forest can far exceed this (c_above 150-300); dry sclerophyll is lower (30-60). Use FullCAM / NCAS for Australian work.

context.assumptions: AGB ~130 t d.m./ha x 0.47; R:S 0.29 (conifer); higher litter accumulation

records.caveats: Managed Pinus radiata plantation c_above swings 10-120 with rotation age; use a rotation-average or stand-age map if the model is sensitive.

context.soil_depth_for_c_soil: 0-30 cm (boreal soils hold much more in deeper peat / O horizons)
context.assumptions: AGB ~30 t d.m./ha x 0.47; R:S 0.24-0.39; large litter + soil pool

cover.label_source: Temperate / Mediterranean shrubland, heath, mallee scrub

context.study_area: IPCC Vol 4 (shrubland / other wooded land); R:S high for woody shrubs
IPCC Vol 4 Ch 6 (grassland); herbaceous R:S 1.5-4 so c_below > c_above
context.assumptions: peak standing AGB 2.1-6.1 t d.m./ha x 0.47; SOC ~ native reference (management factor ~1)

records.caveats: Almost all grassland carbon is in the soil and roots. c_above is small and seasonal - many InVEST studies set it 1-3. Degradation lowers c_soil (management factor 0.7-0.95).

context.study_area: IPCC Vol 4 Ch 5; SOC = reference x F_LU(long-term cultivated ~0.69-0.80) x F_MG x F_I
context.assumptions: standing crop biomass is small and transient

records.caveats: c_soil is the pool that changes under cropland conversion / BMPs: conventional-till long-term cropland ~0.7 x native SOC; no-till + residues raises F_MG toward 1.0-1.1. Perennial / tree crops carry more c_above (10-40).

cover.label_source: Vegetated inland wetland (herbaceous, peat-forming where perennial)

records.caveats: Wetland soil carbon is highly variable and depth-dependent; if peat is present the 0-30 cm figure badly understates the true stock. Use the IPCC Wetlands Supplement for drained/rewetted scenarios.

cover.label_source: Bare ground, sealed surfaces, open water

records.caveats: Settlement soil still holds some carbon (green space, sealed-over former soil); IPCC settlement SOC often kept near reference x 0.8. Water = 0 in all pools.
